n: Drug Trafficking and Precursor Chemicals (incl. Synthetic Opioids)
ds: Production and trafficking of illicit drugs, diversion of precursor chemicals and sale of synthetic opioids, generating cash proceeds that are placed and moved through retail accounts, trade, couriers and professional money launderers. Chemical and equipment purchases, online sales and pill-press activity are additional signals.

src.t: UNODC, World Drug Report (annual; specify year)
INCB, Precursors and Chemicals Frequently Used in the Illicit Manufacture of Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (annual report; specify year)

cn.rt: Drug cash placed as many small deposits into retail accounts then moved on digitally; lifestyle spend funded by cash.

rat: Cash deposits from multiple locations, precursor purchases and IVTS/trade.

ind.n: Structured cash deposits across many branches by multiple people
ind.cx: Many low-value cash deposits into one account from different locations, often followed by wires out.
ind.ds: Cash is deposited in several locations, channels or accounts on the same day or over a short period so that no single deposit stands out.
ind.cn: Cash deposits split across branches, ATMs or accounts

ind.n: Bulk purchases of precursor chemicals or lab equipment
ind.cx: Customer buys large chemical quantities, pill presses or glassware inconsistent with stated business.
ind.fp: Industrial and academic buyers legitimately purchase chemicals.
ind.ds: Customer buys large chemical quantities, pill presses or glassware inconsistent with stated business.

ind.n: Import-export firms trading chemicals with unusual consignees
ind.cx: Importers deal with unfamiliar overseas parties in high-risk corridors for precursor sources.
ind.fp: Chemical trade is large and lawful.
ind.ds: Importers deal with unfamiliar overseas parties in high-risk corridors for precursor sources.

ind.n: Cash couriering or bulk cash seizures linked to customer
ind.cx: Customer or associates tied to seized cash or declarations.
ind.fp: Cash is legal to carry within limits.
ind.ds: Customer or associates tied to seized cash or declarations.

ind.cx: Payments settled by matching transactions in different countries without cross-border transfers.
ind.ds: Reciprocal or offsetting payments occur between counterparties or operators in different countries with no direct value transfer.
ind.cn: Mirror or offsetting transactions between jurisdictions

ind.n: Proceeds spent on assets, vehicles or in casinos and then converted
ind.cx: Lifestyle spending and asset purchases funded by cash.
ind.fp: Lifestyle may come from legitimate income.
ind.ds: Lifestyle spending and asset purchases funded by cash.

ind.n: Dark-web or social media sales with crypto or payment app proceeds
ind.cx: Receipt of numerous small payments from unrelated persons and crypto conversions to cash.
ind.ds: Informal sellers or operators advertise online and collect payment through payment apps, crypto or unlabelled payments.
ind.cn: Illicit sales or services advertised on social media or marketplaces with app or crypto payments

ind.n: Pharmacy, clinic or online pharmacy with abnormal opioid volumes
ind.cx: Dispensing, imports or payments exceeding peers for controlled substances.
ind.fp: Specialist clinics may have high volumes.
ind.ds: Dispensing, imports or payments exceeding peers for controlled substances.

ind.n: Shell companies buying pill presses or tableting equipment
ind.cx: New firm purchases machines and packaging with no production site.
ind.ds: Recently incorporated entity or group of entities with generic business descriptions shows significant turnover or purchases soon after formation.
ind.cn: Newly formed entity with vague purpose and large flows

ctl.n: Fan-in, fan-out and funnel account detection
ctl.ds: Detects accounts receiving from many unrelated senders, or sending to many beneficiaries, followed by consolidation or onward movement. It surfaces collector, funnel and mule structures.

Applies targeted enhanced checks to customer types or sectors known to be vulnerable to misuse, such as cash-intensive trades, money service businesses, high-value dealers, professional services, charities or waste handlers. Questions and evidence are tailored to how the sector normally operates.

Requires end-user statements, authenticates their signatories, verifies licences and sites, and obtains post-delivery reports for goods and funds. It confirms that goods or funds reach the stated end use.

Screens customers, owners, counterparties, vessels, dealers and addresses against sanctions, enforcement and restricted-party lists at onboarding and ongoing, using fuzzy matching and secondary identifiers. Potential matches are held for adjudication before service or funds are released.
Screens goods descriptions, HS codes and items against export-control, precursor and procurement watch lists, with access to technical review. It catches proliferation-sensitive and restricted goods.

Alerts on unusual countries, corridors, deposit locations and geolocation dispersion relative to the customer profile or on activity near designated risk regions. It focuses review on geographic anomalies.

Prohibits or caps cash for purchases, loans, donations and settlement above a set value, requiring documented non-cash methods and threshold reporting for dealers. It removes a low-traceability payment route.

ctl.n: Cash exchange, declaration and courier checks
ctl.ds: Collects identification for cash exchange, cross-checks cross-border cash declarations, screens freight, mail and cash-in-transit use and applies courier intelligence. It addresses bulk cash movement across borders.

ctl.n: Law enforcement request handling and liaison
ctl.ds: Handles law-enforcement, tax-authority and customs requests promptly, reviews related accounts and maintains rapid contact points. It supports investigations and asset recovery while keeping responses consistent.

Investigates linked clusters and networks of accounts as one case, including broker networks and accounts connected to seizures or requests, rather than reviewing accounts individually. It disrupts organised activity that single-account review would miss.

Detects funds that return to their origin or loop between linked parties through reciprocal, matched, netted or round-trip flows using graph analysis and account comparison. It exposes artificial turnover and loan-back structures.

Briefs front-line, onboarding and investigation staff on current red flags, typologies and escalation routes, including sector-specific patterns and professional-enabler behaviours. It improves recognition of suspicious activity that rules alone cannot see.

ctl.n: Lifestyle and high-value purchase consistency review
ctl.ds: Compares observed spending, luxury and asset purchases and personal-type use of business funds with documented income and wealth during periodic reviews and alerts. It highlights unexplained affluence that may indicate illicit income.
Traces exposure of deposit and withdrawal addresses to illicit clusters and screens wallets with risk-scored alerts. It reveals on-chain exposure.
Model that scores inbound-then-outbound pass-through, new-payee churn, counterparty diversity and profile mismatch to flag likely mule accounts. It prioritises accounts for review and restriction.

Compares actual activity with the customer's declared profile, history and peers and alerts on material or trend-breaking deviation, usually as a contextual signal. It catches change that rules on fixed thresholds miss.

Monitors merchant-level patterns such as ticket size, refund, void and chargeback rates, descriptor mismatch and cross-merchant flows. It identifies transaction laundering, bust-out and illicit merchants.
